clue.text: A jolly old fellow in the last war

parts.note: a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
old means aged
a fellow of a college is a don

explanation.surface: An elderly man reminisces about serving in the most recent war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the old fellow, but it is the slang word for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names the final battle at the end of the world, so it is the war to end all wars.

clue.text: A French cleric's notes

parts.note: musical notes are named by the letters A to G, and three of them are taken here

explanation.surface: Someone is looking at the written notes of a priest in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'). 'A' gives its own letter, and 'notes' gives three more note names, B, B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a priest or monk without other title is addressed by this word, cognate with abbot.

clue.text: Bunk for romp in springtime

indicators.note: in tells us the romp sits inside the word for springtime

parts.note: May is a spring month
a lark is a bit of fun or a romp

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off for a frolic when the weather turns warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is short for bunkum, nonsense, which is what this American slang word means.

clue.text: Where all the world's a stage?

definitions.text: Where all the world's a stage?

parts.words: Where all the world's a stage?
parts.note: quoting Shakespeare's line from As You Like It, read literally: a theatre named after the world, which was where his plays were staged

explanation.surface: A question echoing Shakespeare's famous line about life as theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The playhouse on London's Bankside, where Shakespeare's company performed, was named for the world itself, so the 'world' there really was a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's company playhouse in Southwark carried the name of the round world, making it literally the world's stage.

clue.text: Fight, being sound as a bell

definitions.meaning: a heated argument or scrap, informally
the chiming noise a bell makes

explanation.surface: A boxer in a bout is as fit as a fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a brawl is called by the same imitative word as the chime of a church bell.

clue.text: Haunt of drunken bosses

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters of bosses are staggering about out of order

explanation.surface: A bar frequented by inebriated managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunt' looks like a noun (a hangout of drunks) but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To preoccupy someone's mind constantly is to prey on it as a ghost would.

clue.text: Uncivilised person won Ethel's heart

parts.note: won means got, as in got a prize

indicators.note: heart picks out the central letter of the name Ethel

explanation.surface: A barbarian captured the affections of a woman named Ethel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic tribes who sacked Rome became a byword for barbarians and boors.

clue.text: Head giving former pupil part of Bible

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: A headmaster asks an old boy to read a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher, but it is the heads side of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a coin bearing the monarch's head is its front side, opposite the reverse.

clue.text: Workers who bring in spiders?

definitions.meaning: long-legged arachnids related to spiders, also called daddy-long-legs

explanation.surface: Labourers bring some spiders indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: These creatures are arachnids but not true spiders, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm hands reap crops at the end of summer; the same name is given to long-legged arachnids.

clue.text: Traveller in gondola otherwise is on boat going round lakes

indicators.note: going round means the shuffled letters surround the lakes
otherwise asks for the letters of is on boat to be arranged another way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, so lakes give LL

explanation.surface: A Venetian tourist goes the long way round the lagoons by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges IS ON BOAT into BAOONIST, and 'going round' puts it around LL. A gondola is also the basket hung under a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is also the passenger basket under an aerial craft, so its traveller is an aeronaut.

clue.text: Having recovered from multiple deliveries

definitions.meaning: no longer troubled by, as in getting past an illness
in cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A mother is recovering after giving birth to twins or more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler delivers balls in sets of six, each set having this name.
explanation.definitionFit: We say someone is past an illness this way; a cricket set of six balls has the same name.

clue.text: Noted sailor, engaged, buckled at the knees

definitions.text: Noted sailor, engaged, buckled at the knees

parts.words: Noted sailor, engaged, buckled at the knees
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme seafarer who went to sea with silver buckles on his knee and will come back to marry the singer

explanation.surface: A famous seaman, newly betrothed, felt his legs give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to music; 'buckled' means wearing buckles, not collapsing. In the English song he has 'silver buckles on his knee' and will 'come back and marry me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional English rhyme tells of a sailor gone to sea with silver buckles, promised in marriage to the singer.

clue.text: It's British Rail that's providing this fare from France

parts.note: BR was the abbreviation for the former British Rail network
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: The railway's buffet car is offering French food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a train ticket price, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft creamy cheese from the region east of Paris is a classic French food.

clue.text: Nightclub sure to change address

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A club certainly needs to move to new premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges SURE into URSE. 'address' suggests a location, but here it means a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech, and a learned talk or lecture on a subject is the same thing.

clue.text: Random examinations detect threats to king

parts.note: to spot something is to detect it
in chess, a check is an attack on the king

explanation.surface: Unannounced inspections uncover plots against the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Unannounced inspections chosen at random are made to catch problems by surprise.

clue.text: Terribly happy individual that accepts change to make connections

definitions.text: that accepts change to make connections

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of happy are badly disturbed

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A cheerful person welcomes change in order to network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges HAPPY into PAYPH. 'change' means coins, and 'connections' are telephone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated telephone takes loose coins in return for putting a call through.

clue.text: Argue against goal

definitions.meaning: to protest or disagree with something

explanation.surface: A player disputes a scored goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise opposition, and an aim or purpose is a target pursued.

clue.text: Incentive needed after spree in plant

indicators.note: needed after places the incentive word behind the word for spree

parts.note: a lark is a carefree bit of fun
a spur is an incentive

explanation.surface: Someone needs motivation following a binge at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is a flower, the delphinium relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden flower with spurred blue blooms, related to the delphinium.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's writing on the wall

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of Hatter are crazily jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland scrawls graffiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' reads as the Wonderland character, but 'Mad' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing on the wall is a sign of approaching doom, a menace or warning.

clue.text: Hot-rod driver?

parts.note: not a speeding car enthusiast but a worker who hammers heated metal pins into girders

explanation.surface: A question about someone who drives a souped-up car.
explanation.walkthrough: Shipyard and steelwork rivets were driven in red-hot, so the person hammering them drove hot rods.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who hammers red-hot metal pins to fasten plates together drives them home.

clue.text: Gather together land to make a killing

parts.note: to mass is to gather together
an acre is a measure of land

explanation.surface: A speculator buys up land in order to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a killing' suggests making a fortune; here 'to make' is a link, and 'a killing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughter of many people at once is a large-scale killing.

clue.text: Praise and honour people breaking record

indicators.note: breaking means the honour and people split the record word open

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
men means people

explanation.surface: Applause and awards go to athletes who break a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak approvingly of someone is to praise them.

clue.text: God no longer giving saint a 'shock

parts.note: a turn is a sudden shock, as in 'it gave me a turn'

explanation.surface: A deity stops frightening a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' makes the definition a god no longer worshipped: the old Roman god of agriculture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of sowing and agriculture is a figure of ancient religion, now unworshipped.

clue.text: Pedestrian carries protests in bag

indicators.note: carries means the pedestrian word holds the protests inside it

parts.note: pedestrian, as an adjective, means dull, uninspired, which is hack writing
to protest innocence is to aver it, so protests give avers

explanation.surface: A walker carries placards in a rucksack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective meaning dull, as in hack work.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas bag carried on the back by walkers and soldiers is a type of rucksack.

clue.text: Doctor on morning rounds

indicators.note: on puts the doctor after the morning word, read as following it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor does a hospital round before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests a doctor's ward visits, but means rounds of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds are bullets or cartridges, and this is the informal word for ammunition.

clue.text: Last stop

explanation.surface: The final halt on a route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective (final) but is a verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure and to remain both mean to keep on, and staying put is halting.

clue.text: Winning shot by England opener

parts.note: in cricket a cut is a shot played square of the wicket

indicators.note: opener picks the first letter of England, as an opening batsman goes in first

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman plays the shot that wins the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' looks like part of the cricket scene but is the definition, meaning charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning ways are charming ones, and charming in looks is attractive or sweet.

clue.text: One doesn't stay ill

parts.note: read as someone who doesn't stay in hospital while ill, attending for treatment and going home

explanation.surface: Someone recovers quickly from sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quick recovery; really it is a hospital visitor not admitted overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital patient treated without being admitted for an overnight stay.

clue.text: Runs into agent that's very active

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the agent word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A secret agent who is sprinting is very energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and lively, especially of an older person, is being very active.

clue.text: China normally isn't so hostile

parts.note: China is rhyming slang for a mate (china plate), and a mate is usually not antagonistic

explanation.surface: A remark about China's foreign policy being unusually aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a china is a pal, who would normally be friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and unwelcoming are synonyms: the opposite of how a pal behaves.
